I now have enough to answer.

## How an edit on disk gets picked up

A running Agentic HIL MCP server parses its configuration once at startup and never reloads automatically (`src/agentic_hil/mcp.py`, `src/agentic_hil/configreload.py` module docstring). Picking up a file edit requires an explicit call:

- Over MCP: `project_config_reload_description` (no arguments), dispatched by `ToolService.reload_description` in `src/agentic_hil/tools.py:894`.
- At a shell: `agentic-hil config-reload`, implemented by `config_reload()` in `src/agentic_hil/cli.py:4726`, which previews the same thing without mutating a live server.

The actual work is `reload_description()` in `src/agentic_hil/configreload.py:291`:
1. It re-runs `load_authoritative_config()` on the workspace to get the disk version (`disk`), the same loader used at startup.
2. It refuses if the resolved config path has moved (`_relocated_refusal`) — that would rebind the server to a different project.
3. It builds a new configuration via `merged_description(existing, disk)` (`configreload.py:221`), which takes only four sections from disk — `target`, `debuggers`, `com_ports`, `can_buses` (each entry's own `permissions:` block excluded) — and carries every other section, including all permissions, over unchanged from the object parsed at startup. It re-validates permission-dependent pinning on the *composed* object.
4. `ToolService.reload_description()` then does one atomic swap: `self._swap_config(reloaded)` (`tools.py:943`), which replaces `self.config` and pushes the new config into the coordinator, backend, artifacts, and COM/CAN collaborators — no field-by-field mutation of a live object.

Permissions are never re-read by this path; only a full server restart adopts a changed `permissions` block (or `version`, `workspace_root`, `state_root`, etc. — the full list is documented in `NOT_RELOADED_SECTIONS` in `configreload.py`).

## What refuses the reload while a run is open

`ToolService.reload_description()` gathers `open_holds = self.open_hardware_holds()` (`tools.py:1133`) before calling `reload_description()`. `open_hardware_holds()` returns non-`None` if either a declared run is active (`self.coordinator.run_status()["run_active"]`) or any hardware lease is held outside a run (`self.coordinator.leases`), covering the case where a COM/CAN session outlives `bench_run_stop`.

If `open_holds` is truthy, `reload_description()` (the function in `configreload.py:291`) short-circuits at the `if open_holds:` check and returns `None, _open_run_refusal(existing, open_holds)` (`configreload.py:412`), with `error_type = "config_reload_in_open_run"` (`RELOAD_IN_OPEN_RUN_ERROR`, `configreload.py:108`). The refusal explains that the held names must keep meaning the same physical board mid-run, so nothing is re-read and the run is left untouched. The same function also refuses on an unresolved quarantine/incident via `_unresolved_incident()` (`tools.py:921`), for the analogous reason that an operator is about to be asked to physically check a device by name.
